venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU — inside Faulkner’s call, inside White’s trade
dek: What the coordinator is trying to do, and why the snap looks the way it does. Faulkner’s huddle. White’s nickel. The plays that explain the system.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — Charles has not approved publish. Fan rail stays empty.
headline: Faulkner’s call is width, then Baugh, then the easy throw. White’s call is nickel, four, and the deep ball is dead — he will live with the hitch. That is the night.

offense.kicker: Buster Faulkner — the call in his headset
offense.body:
Faulkner told you the identity in the spring: run it when everybody in the stadium knows you are going to run it, and throw it at a high level. Saturday is that sentence made into snaps.

The card is 12 — two tight ends, Singleton and Wilson, Baugh. That is the heavier look he can go to. What he sent out vs FAU is 11. One back. One tight end. Three wide. Shotgun. 2x2 or trips. He wants the defense stretched so the box cannot load for Baugh without leaving a receiver alone. Singleton starts. Brown is the one they keep throwing to. That is a choice. Width over an extra hat.

They huddle. He wants the call in and the picture clean. He is not playing hurry-up to hide a young offense. He is playing on his terms.

Here is the sequence in his head.

First down: give it to Baugh. Inside zone — the line steps one way, Baugh reads the first hat. If the front clogs, the bounce is already built in. That is not a new play. That is the same call with a different cut. The 18 and the 61 are that read winning. When they get to the paint, he changes the blocking, not the back: puller, power, pads through the pile. The 6-yard score. He told you he would run it when you knew it. He did.

Now the defense has a problem. Sit down for Baugh and the receiver in front of you is uncovered. That is why the next call is hitch. Philo’s job is get it out now. Brown’s 49 is the system, not a bomb. Caught at midfield. First man misses. He runs. Wilson’s chains are the same call to the other side. If the corner gives you the back line in the red zone, the call flips to fade — Stockton, pylon, placed. If they sit the linebackers, the tight end is the answer in the middle. Harpring, 19. Clark’s 10 is a drag underneath the same idea: someone is crossing, someone is sitting, Philo throws the open one.

When the run is real and the safety cheats down, Faulkner takes the top off. Max protect. Abrams, go, right sideline, 63. Brown later, same side, 33. That is the shot he earned. He does not open drives hunting it.

The changeups are still him talking. Empty at the 3: nobody in the backfield, five out. He is asking the edges to declare. They climb the pocket. Contain is gone. Philo keeps. That keep is live because he emptied it. Fourth-and-1 at midfield: under center, sneak, no debate. Brown as a runner to the left — same width, now the receiver is the run. Clark is the second back when Baugh is done, not a gadget package. Jones Jr. closes the night.

What you should see next week: 11, huddle, Baugh on first down. If Campbell sits, hitch. If they load it, the go is coming.
bullets: Identity: run it when they know it. Then the throw is easy.
Card is 12. The call vs FAU is 11 — stretch the field, leave a man free.
Baugh first: zone, bounce if it clogs, power in the paint.
Hitch when they sit. Fade when they give the pylon. Go when the safety cheats the run.
Empty keep, sneak, Brown as a runner — same headset, different ask.

defense.kicker: Brad White — the trade in his headset
defense.body:
White’s install is an odd front with a JACK on the edge and a STAR on the slot. What he played vs FAU is nickel: four down, two linebackers, extra DB on the slot. FAU is no-huddle spread. He is not asking two linebackers and a three-down front to match five skill. He puts Kanye Clark on the slot, Woods and McCray as stand-up edges, Graham and Chiles behind, Thornton and Coleman deep. The front matches the offense he is seeing.

Here is the trade he is making.

Take away the explosive. Corners sit off. Rush four. Do not empty the shell. Make Veltkamp hold it. If he holds it, you win — Coleman jumps the late throw on third-and-10, drive dead at the 6. If he ducks it, you win — A-gap heat, Johnson high-points it. Those two takeaways are the call working. Four-man rush. Zone behind it. He is not blitz-happy. He is waiting.

What he is willing to give is the hitch, the flat, and the out. Five, six, eight yards. Tackle them. Get off the field on third. That is why FAU can complete a pile of throws and never look like they have a bomb. They are taking what he is giving. When the slot is late, that throw is free. When the tackle is missed, that throw is a first down. Two interceptions and long drives in the same night is not a mystery. It is the trade getting expensive.

The snaps he loses tell you the jobs.

Goal line: he packs the box. He is saying there is no bounce, no edge, you have to win the phone booth. Ervin still walks in. The fit is there. The plane is not.

Third-and-goal: same four-man idea, stand-up edges. Veltkamp feels it, leaves the pocket, dives the pylon. The edge’s job in this front is stay home. Contain is the call. That score is the call losing.

The fade: all night the corners have cushion. Late, Valsin stacks Flowers and wins the back line. Same family as Stockton the other way. If you sit off to kill the deep ball, you have to win that one when they fade you.

Graham filling the hole is the linebacker doing the job the lineman left. McCloud is the interior push that makes the duck. Bett strips it in the fourth — the rush finally finishes.

Sumrall said atrocious at times. The film version of that sentence: the front is right for spread. The trade is live. The slot and the edge have to be cleaner or Campbell will take the same five-yard throws and the same scramble.

What you should see next week: nickel again. Four and wait. The jobs are the slot and the edge. Do not let the cushion become a drive.
bullets: Install is odd. Saturday is nickel — the front matches FAU’s spread.
The trade: kill the deep ball, rush four, live with the hitch.
Coleman and Johnson are the wait paying off. The long drives are the hitch they gave.
Lost snaps: phone booth, contain, fade. Those are jobs, not bad luck.
Campbell is hurry-up. Same two spots: slot and edge.

specials.kicker: Specials — he left them out there
specials.body: Fourth-and-4 from the FAU 35. Faulkner can go for it. He lets Durkin from 53 instead. That is a coordinator leaving the offense on the field and still taking the points. Clean. 17–0. No punt.
bullets: Durkin 53 on fourth-and-4. They took the points.

keys: Faulkner: 11 for width. Baugh when they know it. Hitch when they sit. Go when they cheat.
Empty keep and the sneak are him asking the edges and the pile to declare.
White: nickel vs spread. Four and wait. Deep ball is dead. Hitch is the tax.
The tax got expensive when the slot was late and the edge left the pylon.
Campbell: same offense look, same two defensive jobs.

nextWeek.look: They will go hurry-up at the slot. Faulkner will still be 11 and Baugh. White will still be nickel and four. Win the hitch. Stay home on the edge.
